title: The Depression: 1934 job riots and the soup lines in New York
summary: Albert was touring in 1934 but saw soup lines in New York and shared a cheap meal with Ben Barth.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I noticed something in the newspaper yesterday, I guess it was a light, January the 1st, 1934, they told about 1,200 jobless men storming the Court County courthouse. Do you remember that at all?
The 34? I wasn't here, I was traveling.
So you didn't see all that trouble with the men storming the county courthouse, wanting jobs, marching on Washington, those troubles, do you remember any of that?
No, I don't, I wasn't here like I said before, I was traveling east with the band.
Well, any place in the country, did you ever run first jobless men?

No, in New York during the Depression, I've seen them on the soup line. And incidentally, Ben Barth, who had chosen universal attractions, he and I were close friends and we both shared a dinner together. In one of these soup lines, we bought a hamburger and a hot dog and a glass of wheat, absolutely about 158 cents. And since then Ben Barth has become million men, and failed universal attractions.
